title: Subnet tiler & egress-policy sentinel (Terraform operator)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a Terraform-backed operator that reconciles subnet tiling, route table consistency, and egress gateway (NAT/IGW) posture for Private (VPC) deployments. The operator should be usable as a composable Terraform module for customers deploying Redwood Private. Goals: deterministic subnet tiling across AZs, idempotent route table and route propagation, automatic NAT/IGW failover wiring, declarative VPC Endpoint provisioning with policy attachments, and a lightweight sentinel that runs periodic synthetic health checks and emits findings to the Console. The operator must support safe upgrades (canary apply, drift detection, and rollback hooks) and integrate with existing upgrade pipelines and monitoring dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes clear variables for az_distribution, subnet_role_map (public/private/db/infra), cidr_tiling_strategy (per-az/prefix-based), and nat_strategy (single-igw-per-az | centralized-nat-gateway)
Module produces deterministic names and tags for subnets and route tables to avoid drift on re-apply
Route table reconciliation detects missing or extra routes compared to desired state and repairs without requiring manual intervention
NAT/IGW failover works: if a NAT gateway in an AZ is unhealthy, traffic is routed to healthy fallback per policy; test plan demonstrates failover within configured SLO
VPC Endpoints (S3, DynamoDB, ECR, Secrets Manager) can be declared with resource policies; endpoints verify policy attachment and emit warnings when permissive
Operator includes a synthetic probe job that validates egress path, endpoint access, and DNS resolution; probe results are forwarded to Console telemetry and a Grafana dashboard
Upgrade flow: canary apply to single AZ, health checks pass for 30m, automatic rollout to remaining AZs; rollback triggers on repeated probe failures
Module includes migration helper (terraform import scripts and mapping) for customers with existing VPCs
Comprehensive unit and integration tests exist: terraform plan/unit tests, k8s operator e2e (simulated failover), and chaos scenario for route drift
technical_notes:
Implementation approach:
1) Terraform module core: implement tiling logic using a small decision module (local values) that translates a base CIDR + tiling strategy to per-AZ subnets; expose stable name templates and tags.
2) Route reconciliation: providing an 'intent' S3 object (or tfstate-derived map) consumed by an operator which compares cloud routes and repairs via AWS SDK when drift is detected. Keep repairs idempotent and rate-limited.
3) NAT/IGW wiring: support two modes - zonal NAT (recommended) and centralized NAT for cost-sensitive workloads. Implement health-check integration (CloudWatch synthetic pings) and a controller that flips route table associations to fallback NAT when needed.
4) VPC Endpoints: terraform resources with optional policy attachment. Add a linter that flags overly broad endpoint IAM/VPC policies.
5) Operator & health sentinel: lightweight controller (Go) deployed as part of the private control plane that periodically runs probes and reports to the Console via telemetry endpoint.
6) Safe upgrade hooks: pre/post apply scripts, canary AZ toggles, and a rollback controller that re-applies last-known-good route assignments.
7) Testing: unit tests for tiling algorithm and policy linter, a mocked AWS integration test suite, and a makefile target to run local end-to-end using localstack for CI.
Migration notes: provide mapping tool to discover existing subnets and generate terraform import statements; include guidance for overlapping CIDR ranges and renaming strategy.
